questions.q: According to Lynch, what should you invest in?
a: Companies whose business you understand
Industries that everyone is talking about
Stocks trading at the lowest prices
Startups with no revenue yet
questions.why: The overview says Lynch's approach comes down to putting money into companies you understand.

A stock that pays ten dividends a year
A fund that holds ten different industries
A company with ten products on the market

questions.q: Why might a dull or funny company name be a good sign?
a: Wall Street may overlook it, so it stays undiscovered
Dull names are protected by law
Funny names attract institutional buyers
A name has no effect on stock performance
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a dull or funny name may keep Wall Street from noticing a stock too early.

questions.q: Which trait does Lynch list as a warning sign?
a: A hot industry that everyone is chasing
Recurring customers who keep buying
A niche that competitors ignore
Insiders buying shares of the company
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists a hyped industry as one of five warning signs to avoid.

questions.q: How does Lynch classify slow growers?
a: Large companies in mature industries
Small firms growing 20 percent a year
Companies recovering from bankruptcy
Firms whose value lies in hidden assets
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes slow growers as large companies in mature industries that grow slowly.
